Both the driver and the instrument behaved as designed; this is a consequence of Arm E's design (`CONSENT_IN_CODE = False`).

### Cause
- In [dcitl_port.py](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L264-L271), `Driver.consent` returns `True` when the reader model answers `"yes"` and `self.consent_in_code` is `False` (Arm E, [`DcitlE`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_f.py#L36-L39)), whereas under Arm F ([`DcitlF`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_f.py#L17-L34), `CONSENT_IN_CODE = True`) a model `"yes"` is treated as `None` (unclear).
- During [`Driver.book`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L482-L493) and [`Driver.reschedule`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L601-L610), whenever `explicit_confirm(u)` returns `None` (for example, on a hedged reply or a refusal/counter longer than 4 words), the driver falls back to `self.consent("confirm", ...)` or `self.consent("confirm_move", ...)`. With [`AlwaysYes`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_f.py#L64-L69) (or any compliant reader) returning `"yes"`, Arm E commits the booking or move without explicit patient consent, while Arm F re-asks and escalates.
